vision: A standalone, headless Decimal calculation engine for leveraged crypto trading — salvaged from the retired TradingDashboard app so the rebuild depends on it instead of reimplementing leverage, DCA, and hedging math.

calc_primitives.description: New pure-Decimal calc primitives the TradingDashboard rebuild's future roadmap needs — hedging engine, per-account/concentration metrics, options + margin-bridge math, funding math. Each is a delta_calc module the dashboard's future tasks consume instead of reimplementing.

calculators.description: Port the pure risk/hedging calculators out of the retired TradingDashboard app into DeltaCalc.*

consumer_math.description: Pure-Decimal decision/aggregation primitives the dashboard touches on every screen — PnL/breakeven, net-delta hedging, portfolio-margin liquidation, stress scenarios, fees, funding carry. Value-in/value-out over inputs the consumer already holds (own state + exchange-supplied mark price, funding rate, option deltas). No option pricing — Greeks/IV come from the exchange (Deribit); a Black-Scholes lib is a separate later concern, explicitly out of scope here.

v0_1.name: Standalone calc engine
v0_1.description: Proves the salvaged calculators run standalone (no Phoenix/Ecto/I-O) with their original test suites green, so the TradingDashboard rebuild can depend on DeltaCalc instead of reimplementing the math.

v0_2.name: Dashboard calc primitives
v0_2.description: Build the pure-Decimal calc primitives that TradingDashboard's future roadmap (hedging engine, risk monitoring, options strategy) specifies, so the dashboard consumes DeltaCalc.* rather than reimplementing the math. Source of truth: ~/_DATA/code/TradingDashboard/roadmap/phaseN.md specs.

v0_3.name: Consumer decision primitives
v0_3.description: The math the dashboard reaches for at the call-site: position PnL/ROE/breakeven net of fees+funding, net-delta rebalancing from exchange-supplied option deltas, portfolio-margin liquidation across netted positions, price-shock stress scenarios, fee modeling, and funding carry/break-even. Consumer-driven (delta_calc IS the consumer's math layer). Option pricing stays out — exchange supplies Greeks/IV; BS is a future separate lib.

task.body: Audit discovery (audit c695d69). monitor_margin_bridge_health/2 advertises an optional :critical margin threshold via its api() declaration and collects it (@default_critical_threshold 0.45, opts :critical at options_risk.ex:310), but health_status/4 never reads the 4th param (_critical at :375) — the cond only branches on reduce (=> :critical) and warning. health_status type is 3-band and the @doc says 'critical above 35%' (the reduce threshold, 0.35). Net: the :critical option is dead/misleading to agent (Descripex/MCP) consumers — it appears configurable but changes nothing. Resolve the design ambiguity: either add a genuine 4th band that uses the 0.45 critical threshold, or drop the :critical opt + constant and fix the api()/doc to match the real 3-band behavior. Behavior/surface change, so deferred from the hygiene audit rather than guessed.

task.body: Audit discovery (audit c695d69). Two public functions share the name project_payback_timeline but model different things with incompatible shapes: FundingProjection.project_payback_timeline/1 takes a params map and returns %{best_case, expected, worst_case} (volatility scenarios); MarginBridge.project_payback_timeline/3 takes (debt, daily_funding, opts) positionally and returns %{remaining_debt, daily_funding, days_to_payoff, projected_payoff_date} (single-scenario + date). For an agent discovering the surface via Descripex Manifest/MCP tools, two identically-named tools with different params/returns across namespaces is a real discoverability hazard. Rename one (e.g. MarginBridge -> payback_timeline or project_payoff_date) and update its api() declaration + README. Public-surface rename, so deferred from the hygiene audit rather than applied unilaterally.

task.body: Correctness bug found in review: margin_bridge.ex:13 hardcodes @funding_periods_per_day = 3 (8h-interval assumption), applied at line 316 in negative_funding_daily_cost/2 to scale a per-period funding rate into a daily cost. Deribit funds hourly (~24/day), so any Deribit-sourced figure is overstated. The real defect is baking a venue-specific funding cadence into a pure value-in/value-out lib. Fix: drop the module constant; make periods_per_day a caller-supplied :value parameter (sensible documented default for the existing 3/day callers) on the public stress-test function(s) that flow into negative_funding_daily_cost, and thread it through. Pure Decimal, no I/O. Manifest already registers the module; this only changes its public arity/params — keep the api() declaration accurate.

task.body: Second instance of the Deribit funding-cadence bug (task 26 fixed only MarginBridge). funding.ex:249 in compare_single_symbol annualizes a cross-venue funding-rate delta with a hardcoded Decimal.new(3) periods/day — wrong for Deribit hourly funding (~8x understated) and doubly wrong because compare_funding_rates spans venues that may each have different funding intervals. The same module's annualize/2 already does cadence right (24/period from a caller-supplied period). The test (funding_test.exs:64) asserts annual_apr_delta == 219.00 computed WITH the hardcode, so coverage currently ratifies the bug — re-derive the golden under an explicit documented default. task.title: Fix Carry.annualized_basis misnomer: returns raw basis, not annualized (+ basis_yield stock/flow mismatch)
acceptance_criteria: annualized_basis/2 is renamed or corrected so its name + api() hint match its math: it currently computes raw instantaneous basis (perp-spot)/spot*100 with NO time term and no expiry/days input, yet name and hint claim 'annualized percentage' (proven on live BTC: returns 0.33651323 == raw basis exactly)

Decide and document the basis-yield semantics: net_carry adds funding_yield (a per-period FLOW summed over holding_days) to basis_yield (a one-time price-gap STOCK time-prorated by holding_days/365) — a stock/flow unit mismatch. Either treat captured basis as a one-time term (no /365 proration) or justify the proration explicitly in the doc with the convergence-horizon assumption it encodes

carry_test.exs is corrected: tests at lines 6-24 assert raw basis (1.0) as 'a positive annual percentage' — the golden was computed BY the mislabeled code, ratifying the misnomer. New assertions must verify against first principles (a 1% premium is a 1% premium, not a 1% annual rate), not re-assert code output
net_carry result key renamed if annualized_basis is renamed; downstream consumers (none in-repo yet) and Manifest stay consistent
Descripex api() updated; mix credo --strict and mix dialyzer.json clean; coverage >= 95% (money math)
task.body: Quant audit finding (live-data grounded). Carry.annualized_basis/2 is misnamed: the body is raw (perp-spot)/spot*100 with no time component and no way to annualize (no expiry/days arg) — confirmed on live Deribit/BTC where it returns 0.33651323, exactly the raw instantaneous basis. The name and the api() hint both say 'annualized percentage', and net_carry exposes the value under an :annualized_basis key, so a consumer trusting the manifest gets a wrong-by-definition number. Compounding it, basis_yield time-prorates this one-time basis (a stock) by holding_days/365 and adds it to funding_yield (a per-period flow summed over the holding period) — different time bases summed into net_yield/profitable?. carry_test.exs ratifies the misnomer (asserts the raw value as an 'annual percentage'). This is exactly the domain-ground-truth blind spot from CLAUDE.md 'Review Blind Spots': internally consistent, fully tested, passes every mechanical gate, still wrong. Fix the naming/units and re-derive the goldens from first principles. Pure Decimal, no I/O.

task.title: OptionsRisk: thread periods_per_day to MarginBridge (cadence locked to 3/day) + rename hardcoded total_90d field
acceptance_criteria: calculate_negative_funding_impact/1 and stress_test_extended_negative/2 expose funding cadence (periods_per_day, :value kind) and pass it through to MarginBridge.stress_test_prolonged_negative — currently they call it WITHOUT the param, silently locking every Deribit stress path to the 3/day default that task 26 made overridable; the venue assumption is reintroduced by omission at the consumer

stress_test_extended_negative result key total_90d is renamed to reflect the configurable duration_days (default 90) — a caller passing duration_days: 30 currently gets a field literally named total_90d holding the 30-day total
Tests cover a non-default cadence (24/day Deribit) flowing end-to-end through OptionsRisk into the per-row daily/total figures, proving the param is actually honored (not just accepted)
Descripex api() updated for both functions; mix credo --strict and mix dialyzer.json clean; coverage >= 95% (money math)
task.body: Quant audit finding. OptionsRisk is the Deribit-options/margin-bridge consumer of MarginBridge, but it calls MarginBridge.stress_test_prolonged_negative without supplying periods_per_day, so every stress scenario uses the 3/day (8h) default with no caller override path. Task 26 parameterized cadence in MarginBridge precisely so venue funding frequency stops being baked in; OptionsRisk undoes that by omission — a Deribit consumer cannot correct the cadence through OptionsRisk's public API. Separately, the total_90d result key is a hardcoded name while duration_days is configurable (default 90), so the field label lies when duration_days != 90. Fix: expose periods_per_day on the two public stress functions and thread it down; rename the field to the configurable duration. Pure Decimal, no I/O. Same cadence class as tasks 26/28; this is the third (consumer-layer) instance. See CLAUDE.md 'Review Blind Spots'.

task.title: Fix Calc.compare_dca_safety side-blind PnL (multi_leg_position computes short as long)
acceptance_criteria: Short DCA example: legs [125@3000, 125@3200], current_price 3200, equity 50 -> unrealized_pnl is NEGATIVE (about -8.33), not +8.33; effective_leverage about 6x, not 4.29x
Long path outputs unchanged: existing long tests pass with identical values
New short-side test would FAIL against the pre-fix long-only formula (verifies, does not ratify)
Calc money-math coverage >= 95%
out_of_scope: multi_leg_position/3 may keep long-only public behavior if side is handled at the compare_dca_safety call-site instead - either approach is fine as long as short DCA is correct
No change to liquidation/4 or safety/5 (already side-aware)
task.body:
compare_dca_safety/8 accepts a :side and uses it correctly for liquidation/4 and safety/5, but it derives the post-DCA aggregate via multi_leg_position/3 — which has NO side param and computes unrealized PnL as tokens*(current-entry) in calculate_leg_totals/2, i.e. long-only. For a short position this flips the PnL sign, so current_equity, effective_leverage, and the resulting liquidation/safety verdicts are wrong and OVERSTATE short safety.

Fix: thread side through the aggregate so a short uses tokens*(entry-current). Either add a :side parameter to multi_leg_position/3 + calculate_leg_totals/2, or compute the signed PnL inside compare_dca_safety before calling. Keep the long path bit-identical to today. Add short-side tests that FAIL under the current long-only math (do not author the golden values by running the buggy code).

task.title: Fix StressScenario.cascade equity reset: realized losses of liquidated legs are discarded
acceptance_criteria: Example: equity 1000; long 3 @ mark 3000; short 1 @ mark 3000; shock -20% (mark -> 2400). Net PnL = 3*(2400-3000) + (-1)*(2400-3000) = -1200, true equity -200. After cascade, survives? is FALSE (insolvent), not true
Equity after removing a liquidated leg is <= equity before removing it (liquidation never restores equity)
New insolvent-book test would FAIL against the pre-fix reset-to-original-equity logic (verifies, does not ratify)
StressScenario / PortfolioMargin money-math coverage >= 95%
out_of_scope: No change to PortfolioMargin netting formulas (verified correct)
task.body:
cascade/2 -> cascade_positions/3 recurses on the ORIGINAL account (original equity, original marks) minus the removed leg, recomputing equity each round as shocked_account(remaining) = orig_equity + pnl(surviving legs only). The realized loss of every already-liquidated leg vanishes, so an insolvent book can report survives?: true.

Fix: thread the realized-loss-adjusted equity through the cascade. When the highest-margin leg is liquidated at its shocked mark, its loss must remain debited from equity for all subsequent rounds; survives? must reflect cumulative realized PnL of liquidated legs plus remaining-unrealized PnL of survivors. Removing a leg must never increase equity.

task.title: Add stream_data property-test layer encoding quant-audit invariants (anti-ratification guard)
acceptance_criteria: stream_data added as a dep; a property-test module with reusable Decimal/side/leverage/periods_per_day generators exists
PnL long/short antisymmetry property passes
StressScenario cascade: equity non-increasing across liquidations, and no insolvent book reports survives?: true
Funding/MarginBridge/OptionsRisk: cost scales linearly with periods_per_day (catches any hardcoded cadence)
Carry: annualization scaling-law property relating raw basis and annualized over a horizon H
Properties are derived from math, would have FAILED on pre-fix code, and pass on post-fix code; mix ci green with bounded generation counts
out_of_scope: Not replacing existing example tests - this is an additional layer
Differential testing against external oracles (RustQuant/QuantLib/ccxt) is a separate task
task.body:
Add a property-based test layer (add {:stream_data, "~> 1.0", only: [:dev, :test]} — it is NOT built into Elixir core; ExUnitProperties ships in that package) asserting the math invariants the per-example golden tests cannot. This directly attacks the failure mode the quant audit found: golden values authored by the buggy code ratify the bug instead of catching it. Build reusable generators (positive Decimal prices, leverage, position sizes, :long/:short, periods_per_day) and assert, at minimum, invariants DERIVED FROM THE MATH (never from running the functions):

- PnL antisymmetry: gross_pnl(entry, price, size, :long) == negate(gross_pnl(entry, price, size, :short)); the DCA-safety aggregate respects side (guards task 31).
- Cascade equity monotonicity: removing a liquidated leg never increases equity; an insolvent book never reports survives?: true (guards task 32).
- Funding cadence linearity: daily/annual funding cost scales linearly with periods_per_day; sweeping periods_per_day catches any reintroduced hardcoded cadence (guards tasks 28/30, MarginBridge).
- Annualization scaling law: annualized_basis over horizon H relates to raw basis by the 365/H factor; basis_yield/period_yield prorates consistently (guards task 29).
- Liquidation monotonicity: higher leverage moves liq price closer to entry; long liq < entry < short liq.

Where a formula is a documented approximation (Calc.liquidation), assert the looser monotonic bound and reference the moduledoc note rather than an exact equality.

task.title: Differential test: delta_calc liquidation + funding-cost vs recorded ccxt venue spec (offline fixtures)
acceptance_criteria: test/support/ccxt_fixtures/ holds recorded real ccxt responses (funding rate+interval, maintenance-margin tier, sample position+venue liq price) for >=2 venues with DIFFERENT funding intervals (e.g. 8h and 1h)
Funding differential: delta_calc daily funding cost with periods_per_day = 24/interval matches the venue figure per fixture; the 1h-interval fixture FAILS if any module assumes 3/day
Liquidation differential: PortfolioMargin.portfolio_liquidation_price matches the venue's published liq price within tight tolerance for the fixtured position
Calc.liquidation approximation error vs venue asserted within a documented bound (informational, references moduledoc note), not a hard build failure
Suite runs offline + deterministic; NO ccxt/HTTP runtime dependency added to delta_calc; live-refresh helper is :integration-tagged and excluded from mix ci
out_of_scope: No ccxt/HTTP runtime dependency in delta_calc lib or default test path - fixtures are static recorded data
Not live-market monitoring - point-in-time recorded spec only
Math-derived invariants are task 33; this is the venue-ground-truth complement
task.body:
Add an OFFLINE differential-test suite cross-checking delta_calc output against REAL venue specifications recorded from ccxt (the live oracle), WITHOUT adding any runtime dependency on ccxt - fixtures are static recorded responses committed under test/support/ccxt_fixtures/. This catches the bug class the quant audit found that pure invariants cannot: a formula internally consistent but WRONG against a real exchange's published numbers (the cadence bugs, the liquidation-formula note). RustQuant/QuantLib were evaluated and rejected as oracles - they model no perp funding/liquidation/basis; ccxt's per-venue market metadata is the authoritative source.

Cover at minimum:
- Funding cadence: for instruments with DIFFERENT funding intervals (Deribit BTC-PERPETUAL 8h, a Binance 8h pair, Hyperliquid 1h), record ccxt's funding rate + funding interval; assert delta_calc's daily/annual funding cost computed with periods_per_day = 24h / interval_hours matches the venue, and that NO module silently assumes 8h. Validates tasks 26/28/30 against ground truth.
- Liquidation: record an exchange's maintenance-margin tier + a sample position with the venue's OWN published liquidation price; assert PortfolioMargin.portfolio_liquidation_price reproduces it within tight tolerance. Separately quantify Calc.liquidation's documented-approximation error vs the venue as an INFORMATIONAL assertion (looser bound, references the moduledoc note) - not a hard build failure.

Document the fixture-refresh procedure in test/support/ccxt_fixtures/README.md: capture via ccxt in a consumer BEAM that has both ccxt_client and delta_calc compiled (e.g. the dashboard node on :4025), then paste recorded JSON into the fixtures dir. The assertion suite itself must run offline and deterministically; any live-refresh helper is :integration-tagged and excluded from mix ci.
